newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NEW FACES IN ITALY SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW FACES IN ITALY SQUAD.

text.p: Fabrizio Ravanelli and Roberto Baggio were left out of Italy's squad for the four-nation Tournoi de France on Friday.
Three new faces emerged and striker Alessandro Del Piero returned from injury.
Coach Cesare Maldini named a squad of 23 for the tournament, which also involves Brazil, France and England, starting on Tuesday.

Ravanelli, currently with relegated Middlesbrough in England but expected to be moving on shortly, is recovering from injuries that tormented his last few matches of the English season and had been doubtful.
The player had reportedly assured Maldini that he was ready to play but the coach clearly thought otherwise.
Del Piero had been out of the squad since February due to a thigh injury but Maldini was clearly impressed by his form for Juventus in the European Cup final on Wednesday.
Although Juventus lost 3-1 to Borussia Dortmund, Del Piero crafted a fine second half goal.

AC Milan's 1994 World Cup hero Roberto Baggio, who made a memorable return to the national team when he came on as a substitute and scored against Poland in a World Cup qualifier at the end of April, was also left out due to injury.
Baggio suffered a groin strain in a friendly match at the Milanello training ground on Thursday. Milan midfield team mate Stefano Eranio is also out injured.
In their place, Maldini summoned three new faces to join his familiar cast of stalwarts.
Demetrio Albertini and Alessandro Costacurta will be suspended for Italy's next World Cup qualifier against Georgia and Maldini wanted to test possible alternatives.

Vicenza midfielder Giampiero Maini, a goalscorer in his club's historic Italian Cup win against Napoli on Thursday, earned a first call and the first for a Vicenza player since Paolo Rossi 18 years ago.
"I didn't understand, I thought I must be dreaming," was Maini's immediate reaction. "I was speechless."

An even bigger surprise was Piacenza midfielder Eusebio Di Francesco, whose small town club must beat Perugia on Sunday to have any chance of avoiding relegation from serie A but who is set to join Roma next season.
The third completely newcomer was Bologna defender Stefano Torrisi. Like Maini, he has played for Italy at youth level.
Internazionale's in-form Gianluca Pagliuca returned as second choice goalkeeper, replacing Fiorentina's Francesco Toldo who has suffered a poor season.
